subject: Unexpected high consumption on Jan invoice — request for usage breakdown
messages:
From: Lisa Chen <lisa@solargrid.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.com
Cc: eng-ops@solargrid.com
Date: Sat, 14 Feb 2026 09:17:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected high consumption on Jan invoice

Hi Monica,

We just received our January invoice and the token consumption is ~3.6x higher than our internal estimate. I attached the invoice and our internal usage export for Jan. Can you help explain where the extra cost came from?

Quick context: we have a DPA model pinned to rwd-large-v1 and a baseline of ~120M tokens/mo. January shows 430M tokens billed. There were no product changes on our side that we’re aware of.

We’d like:
- A line-item breakdown by route/model and time window (UTC)
- Confirmation whether any fallback to larger models occurred or if streaming retries doubled counts
- Temporary hold on collections for the disputed portion while we investigate (PO/AR team email is finance@solargrid.com)

Thanks,
Lisa Chen
Head of Product Engineering
SolarGrid Inc.

Attachments: Invoice_2026-01_SolarGrid.pdf (pdf), SolarGrid_usage_export_Jan2026.csv (csv)
From: monica_patel@redwood.com
To: Lisa Chen <lisa@solargrid.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 16 Feb 2026 08:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected high consumption on Jan invoice

Hi Lisa — thanks for flagging and for the attachments. I’m looping in Aditya (SE) and Naomi (Billing) to help reconcile quickly.

Action items from our side:
- Aditya will pull per-route per-model token counts and check for model fallback events.
- Naomi will review the invoicing window and meter snapshot we used to generate the bill.
- Monica will request a 14-day billing hold for the disputed amount and confirm AR contact.

Naomi — can you pause the payment collection for the disputed $24,300 portion pending an initial reconciliation?

Lisa — we’ll aim to get a preliminary update within 48 hours.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
monica_patel@redwood.com
From: aditya_rao@redwood.com
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, Lisa Chen <lisa@solargrid.com>
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 17 Feb 2026 10:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected high consumption on Jan invoice

Hi all — I pulled the raw metering logs for SolarGrid for Jan 01 00:00 UTC → Jan 31 23:59 UTC. Initial observations:

- Two short periods of increased traffic on Jan 12 03:20–03:45 UTC and Jan 21 17:10–17:27 UTC where per-minute TPS spiked 8–12x. Those intervals account for ~95M of the extra tokens.
- During the Jan 21 spike we logged several 503 errors from our GPU pool in us-west-2. For a subset of requests we automatically routed to the compatible fallback model rwd-large-ephemeral which has ~1.8x token footprint for the same prompts.
- We also saw a small number (~4.2k) of streaming reconnects where the client retried after a dropped connection. Our metering counts each partial stream as tokens consumed; reconnects added ~6.4M tokens.

So the delta breakdown looks like:
- Normal baseline: ~120M tokens
- Spike events (two burst windows): ~95M tokens
- Fallback model footprint delta: ~60M tokens (estimated)
- Streaming reconnects: ~6.4M tokens
- Misc/rounding: ~3.6M tokens

Total: ~285M extra → billed ~430M.

I’ll attach the per-request CSV extract and the fallback routing logs. The fallback was triggered by capacity fallback policy during the 503s — not by a client-specified model change.

Regards,
Aditya Rao
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, Lisa Chen <lisa@solargrid.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 09:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected high consumption on Jan invoice

Thanks Aditya — that level of detail helps. Per Redwood billing policy, fallbacks and retries are billable (they consume inference capacity), but we do provide goodwill adjustments in cases where platform issues (e.g., 503s) caused sudden spikes and impacted a customer materially.

Given the evidence of two sustained traffic spikes coinciding with GPU pool 503s and automatic fallback routing, I recommend the following:

1) Issue a one-time credit for the estimated fallback footprint delta (we propose a 50% credit on the 60M token delta while we continue to audit logs): credit = price_per_token * 30M tokens → $9,450 credit.
2) Waive charges associated with streaming reconnect tokens that are a direct result of our dropped connections (6.4M tokens) → $2,016 credit.
3) Place the disputed $24,300 on hold for 14 days, pending your finance team's confirmation.

If SolarGrid concurs, we’ll generate a credit memo and adjust the outstanding balance. If you prefer a different split for the fallback credit (e.g., 75%/25%), we can discuss.

Naomi Feldman
Billing Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
naomi_feldman@redwood.com
From: Lisa Chen <lisa@solargrid.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 10:01:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected high consumption on Jan invoice

Monica / Naomi / Aditya — thank you for the quick investigation and the breakdown. The timeline and logs you provided match what our SRE saw (we had an unrelated upstream DB flapping event that triggered a retry storm on Jan 21).

SolarGrid accepts the proposed credits but we'd like to request two things before you issue the memo:
- Please increase the fallback credit to 75% of the 60M token delta due to the fallbacks being a direct consequence of your regional GPU pool instability.
- Include a short post-mortem note describing the root cause and actions to prevent recurrence (we need this for our internal audit).

If you can confirm those two items, we’ll instruct our AP team to release the non-disputed portion of the invoice.

—Lisa
From: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
To: Lisa Chen <lisa@solargrid.com>, monica_patel@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 16:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected high consumption on Jan invoice

Lisa — we can do that. Revised proposal:
- Fallback credit: 75% of 60M tokens = 45M tokens credit → credit amount $14,175.
- Streaming reconnects credit: full removal of 6.4M tokens → $2,016 credit.
- We will issue a credit memo and annotate the Jan invoice; disputed $24,300 will be on hold for 14 days.
- Engineering will provide a short post-mortem (1–2 paragraphs) describing the GPU pool 503s, the automatic fallback behavior, and the mitigation steps (pool sizing and improved backoff on retries). We’ll include the post-mortem as a PDF in the credit memo email.

Expect the credit memo and updated invoice by EOD Feb 20.

Thanks — Naomi
Billing Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
